metadata.note: ai-explainer / claude-hai. ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00 (cold open, answered), B09 (verdict artifact), B10 (handoff) and B11 (outro) only — every body beat illustrates its concept as a native animated Remotion scene (REBUILD LAW). The four source PNGs and their SVG sources are REFERENCE in pantry/, never slotted as media. The script's six sections are split into eight body beats; the split is logged in BUILD-LOG.md. THREE THINGS NOT TO GET WRONG: token bounding is the deliverable and not a detail; read-only is a design decision and not a limitation; and the refused fields are structural and not stylistic. VERTICAL CUT: every beat re-renders from a <pattern>916 portrait composition — a re-layout, never a crop. The narration mp3s are copied from the 16:9 reel, not regenerated, so the two masters are the same edit.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about making this dataset usable by something other than me. Two pieces: a read only server an A I assistant can query directly, and a frozen J S O N contract another system can parse without guessing. Up to now everything here was a script I run and a document I read. Fine for building it. Useless to anyone else.

shot.visual_intent: COLD OPEN LAW: the interface IS the subject this week, so the reel opens inside a client talking to the thing it is about.

show.event: The ask types into the Claude composer.
The result lands ANSWERED with three output lines.

props.segment: Serving the Panel over MCP and Freezing the Signal Contract
props.command: Serve the marks panel over MCP so an assistant can query it directly, and freeze the quarter's numbers into a contract another system can parse. Keep it read-only — and tell me what it has to refuse.
output: 6 read-only tools, none of which writes a mark, a gate or a decision
one query returns 2,151 rows — bounded to 18k characters from 575k
and a signal frozen at 1.0 that refuses 10 field names by name

beats.narration_text: Two deliverables. A server with six tools, none of which writes anything, and a signal file frozen at version one point zero. The hard part was never the protocol. Writing a server that speaks it took an afternoon. The hard parts were size, and what a contract has to refuse.

shot.visual_intent: BLUF names both deliverables and strikes the thing a viewer would assume was hard, so the rest of the reel has somewhere to go.

show.event: The headline sets, then the two pieces land side by side.
A 'the protocol' chip lands and is struck through.

show.at: on 'size, and what a contract has to refuse'
show.event: The real constraints replace it.

props.sparkLine: The protocol was the easy part.
props.headline: Two deliverables, one week.

beats.narration_text: Ask for Databricks' full price history and you get two thousand one hundred and fifty one rows. Five hundred and seventy five thousand characters. Roughly a hundred and forty three thousand tokens. That is larger than most context windows, and useless even where it fits, because a model handed two thousand rows will not read them.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w10-bounding.png. The ratio between the two bars IS the argument, so nothing else on the frame competes with it.

show.at: on 'two thousand one hundred and fifty one rows'
show.event: The full-table bar draws across the frame and lands its char and token counts.
The bounded bar draws beneath it, a fraction of the width.
The reason the size matters lands under both.

props.sparkLine: Larger than the window, and unread inside it.
props.title: One query, two possible answers
props.subtitle: get_marks('Databricks, Inc.') — 2,151 rows available
props.tokenNote: ~4 characters per token is an estimate, not a tokenizer count
props.readNote: A model handed 2,151 rows does not read them. It reads the summary, which describes the WHOLE result set, and pages only if it needs to.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata.json — tools[get_marks]; token figure derived at chars/4

beats.narration_text: So every answer is three parts: a summary describing the whole result set, one bounded page, and a cursor. On that query, eighteen thousand characters instead of five hundred and seventy five thousand. But look at the other five tools. The envelope makes every one of them bigger, by nineteen to forty nine percent. Bounding is not free.

shot.visual_intent: Not in the script or either figure. Both present bounding as a pure win because the one tool they show is the one where it is. This beat is the reel arguing with its own source material.

show.event: The envelope's three parts land as a short list.

show.at: on 'look at the other five tools'
show.event: Six rows land, each with its bounded-versus-whole delta.
The five costlier rows take the count, and the one that pays takes the accent.

props.sparkLine: It pays for itself exactly once.
props.title: The envelope is not free
props.subtitle: bounded response against the same answer serialised whole, per tool
parts: a summary of the WHOLE result set
props.note: It pays for itself on exactly one tool — the one that would otherwise return 2,151 rows, where it saves 97%. That is the trade, and it is worth saying out loud.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata.json — tools[]; the overheads are derived, and asserted

beats.narration_text: Six tools. List the companies, get one company's marks, compare managers on a date, get propagation, get a fund's exposure, and list what is still unresolved. Nothing writes. No tool records a decision, clears a gate, or changes a mark. Earlier I established that a resolution decision needs a named human. A tool a model can call is the opposite of that.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w10-tools.png. SHOW-DON'T-TELL: 'read-only' is drawn as a list of what is ABSENT, because an absence is the claim.

show.event: Six rows land, each with rows returned against rows available.
Three things no tool can do land beneath, as a list of absences.
The reason lands as the beat's closing block.

props.sparkLine: The code proposes. A person still decides.
props.title: Six tools, and none of them writes
props.subtitle: rows returned against rows available, with the response size
props.pagedNote: Red marks the one tool whose answer was paged. Everything else fits whole.
props.whyNote: A resolution decision needs a named human. A tool a model can call to record one is the opposite of that. A model here reads every judgment already made, and sees what is still open. It cannot make one.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata.json — tools[]; measured against the live database

beats.narration_text: The other piece is the signal. Nine top level keys, frozen at version one point zero, and validated before it is ever written to disk. It refuses ten field names outright. Valuation. Market cap. Shares outstanding. Return. Not style, structure. These filings give a fund's share count, never the company's total shares.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w11-contract.png. The refused column is read FROM the emitted file rather than from a list in the figure, so the frame proves the refusal rather than restating it.

show.event: The nine keys the signal carries land in a column.
Ten refused names land opposite, struck as they arrive.
The structural reason lands below both.

props.sparkLine: A contract is what it refuses.
props.title: 9 keys it carries, 10 names it refuses
props.subtitle: schema_version 1.0 · validated before it is written to disk
props.whyNote: N-PORT gives a fund's share count, never the company's shares outstanding, so there is no arithmetic here to a company's value. A field for one would invite a consumer to fill it from elsewhere and inherit that source's error.
props.proof: 9 top-level keys present · 0 refused names present
props.source: SOURCE: signal_example.json, read directly — the key list is the file's own

beats.narration_text: Where a figure is withheld, the reason is a value, not a missing key. Four companies are suppressed this quarter. And two counts here disagree on purpose. The server lists eleven companies. The signal publishes ten. The eleventh has zero marks. An empty answer is still an answer, and the server says so rather than returning nothing.

shot.visual_intent: DOUBLE-CHECK LAW. The 11-versus-10 looks like a defect on any frame that shows both, so the reel reconciles it rather than hoping nobody notices.

show.event: The four suppressed companies land, each carrying a reason rather than a gap.
The two counts land side by side and the difference resolves to one company.

show.at: on 'an empty answer is still an answer'
show.event: The zero-row tool lands with its own summary note.

props.sparkLine: A reason, not a missing key.
props.title: Suppressed is a value
props.subtitle: what the signal does when it will not publish a figure
props.reconcileLabel: two counts that disagree on purpose
props.reconcileNote: The server lists 11 companies because that is the universe it carries. The signal publishes 10 because 1 of them has zero marks. Neither number is wrong; they answer different questions.
props.emptyLabel: and an empty answer is still an answer
props.emptyNote: list_unresolved returns 0 rows and says so in its summary. Nothing is unresolved this quarter. That is a finding, not a blank.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata.json — signal.suppressed, tools[]; counts reconciled at injection

beats.narration_text: The quarterly note is the only prose a model writes here, and it gets the computed figures and nothing else. No database. No tools. I expected one check to be enough: no number that is not in the figures. It was not. A draft passed cleanly and still said one company had the fewest marks, one sentence before saying a different company had the fewest.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w11-guards.png, plus the fourth check the figure predates. FALSIFIABILITY: the beat is the author's own expectation being wrong.

show.at: on 'the computed figures and nothing else'
show.event: What the model has lands beside three things it does not.
The three guards land with the draft that fails each.

show.at: on 'a different company had the fewest'
show.event: The invented-ranking row takes the accent and the contradiction lands beneath it.

props.sparkLine: Every number real. The ranking invented.
props.title: The grounding check passed anyway
props.subtitle: 388 words accepted from groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b after retries

guards.draft: Databricks, Inc. has the lowest number of marks, at 2151.
Figure AI had a maximum spread of null.

fourth.draft: an empty draft passes every content check trivially

props.fourthNote: The fourth check is not in figdata.json — from README.md and narration_script.md — it added after w11-guards.png was drawn, which is why that figure says three.
props.punchNote: Every number in that draft was real, so the grounding check passed. The RANKING was what the model invented, and it contradicted itself inside one paragraph.
props.retryNote: A failed draft goes back to the model with the specific complaint, up to three times.

beats.narration_text: Two things the checks still miss. A draft that came back empty passed every one of them and was recorded as a success, at zero words. And a draft that spelled a number in words went unread, because the check only looked at digits. Then three setup bugs in a row, all invisible from inside the server, all because my test supplied what a real client does not.

shot.visual_intent: The reel's last body beat is its own limits, as in every episode of this series. The three bugs are the author's, and the lesson is stated as a rule rather than an apology.

show.at: on 'recorded as a success, at zero words'
show.event: The two misses land, each with what the check actually read.

show.at: on 'three setup bugs in a row'
show.event: The three land as a stack, then the shape they share.

show.at: on 'what a real client does not'
show.event: The closing block states what none of this shows.

props.sparkLine: A test that withholds what the caller withholds.
props.title: What none of the checks catch

misses.miss: an empty note was accepted as a success
misses.detail: recorded as "0 words" — nothing to fabricate, nothing to rank, no placeholder
"across sixty-one groups" was correct, and would have passed had it been wrong

props.bugsLabel: three setup bugs, all the same shape
bugs: a cwd key the client never applies before resolving the module
a --cwd flag that does not exist on the CLI
a default registration scope that binds the server to whichever directory it ran in
props.lesson: The server's own selftest passed through all three, and so did an in-process protocol test that supplied the working directory itself. A test finds this class of bug only if it WITHHOLDS what the real caller withholds.
notShown: No company valuation. These filings give a fund's share count, never the company's shares outstanding.
Not timely. Filings lag their period end by roughly 55 to 60 days, and the bulk sets lag those again.
Every rendering is labelled model output, not a verified claim — a wrong adjective with a correct number attached still passes.
props.source: SOURCE: not in figdata.json — from README.md and narration_script.md — both misses and all three bugs

beats.narration_text: Week ten on one page. A read only server with six tools, none of which writes a mark, a gate or a decision. One query returns two thousand one hundred and fifty one rows, bounded to eighteen thousand characters from five hundred and seventy five thousand, and the envelope costs more on the other five tools than it saves there. A signal frozen at one point zero with nine keys and ten field names refused by name. And the grounding check passed a draft that invented a ranking, which is why there are four checks now and not one.

shot.visual_intent: Judgment beat. The artifact page is the point (ILLUSTRATE LAW carve-out).

show.event: Five findings stagger in, one per spoken clause.

props.artifactTitle: Serving the Panel over MCP and Freezing the Signal Contract — week 10
props.artifactHeading: What shipped, and what it refuses
artifactLines: A read-only MCP server: 6 tools, none of which writes a mark, clears a gate or records a decision. A resolution decision still needs a named human.
Every answer is bounded twice — 50 rows AND 48,000 characters — because row widths are not uniform. get_marks: 2,151 rows, 18k chars instead of 575k, a 97% cut.
But the envelope COSTS on 5 of the 6 tools, +19% to +49%. It pays for itself on exactly one.
A signal frozen at 1.0: 9 top-level keys, 10 field names refused by name, 4 companies suppressed with a reason rather than a missing key.
The grounding check passed a draft that invented a ranking and contradicted itself in one paragraph. Four checks now, not one — and the fourth is why an empty note no longer counts as a success.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Take a test you trust and find what it supplies that a real caller would not. The working directory. An environment variable. An already running process. Then withhold one and run it again. Mine passed three times before a real client ever reached it.

shot.visual_intent: HANDOFF LAW: a real prompt, read ALOUD verbatim and then discussed. One of exactly two typing beats.
